---
title: "Build Execution"
---

> ⚠️ **Prerequisite**  
> You need an active workspace and application.  
> → Start with [Create Your First Feature](/docs/build/quick-start)

The Build pipeline is the execution path behind every generated change. It turns a requirement into a scoped implementation plan, applies code changes, validates the result, and packages everything as a pull request.

## Why the pipeline matters

Generated code is only useful if it is traceable and reviewable. The pipeline makes the work inspectable by separating intent, repository analysis, implementation, validation, and delivery.

Use this page when you want to understand why a build behaved a certain way or where to look when a build fails.

## Pipeline stages

<Steps>
  <Step title="Requirement analysis">
    Revolte reads the prompt and identifies the desired behavior, affected application areas, likely tests, and possible configuration changes.
  </Step>

  <Step title="Repository analysis">
    Revolte inspects the connected codebase for framework conventions, folder structure, existing helpers, test setup, build commands, and runtime configuration.
  </Step>

  <Step title="Implementation plan">
    The request is decomposed into concrete steps so the generated change remains focused.
  </Step>

  <Step title="Code generation">
    Revolte edits the relevant files and adds new files only when the request requires it.
  </Step>

  <Step title="Validation">
    Revolte runs available checks such as unit tests, integration tests, build commands, linting, or configuration validation.
  </Step>

  <Step title="Pull request delivery">
    The final output is delivered as a pull request with implementation context and validation evidence.
  </Step>
</Steps>

## What Revolte considers

During repository analysis, Revolte should account for:

- Framework and language
- Project structure
- Existing conventions
- Test setup
- Build and start commands
- Runtime configuration
- Service integrations
- Deployment impact

## Example pipeline trace

```txt
Requirement: Add password reset emails.

Analysis:
- Locate auth module
- Find email provider integration
- Add reset-token persistence
- Add request and confirm endpoints
- Add tests for token expiry and invalid token

Output:
- Auth service changes
- Email template or call site
- Tests
- Pull request summary
```

## Failure handling

If the pipeline fails, start with the stage that failed.

| Failed stage | What to inspect |
| --- | --- |
| Requirement analysis | Prompt clarity, missing acceptance criteria |
| Repository analysis | Repository access, branch availability, monorepo root |
| Code generation | Conflicting patterns, missing dependencies |
| Validation | Test output, build logs, lint errors |
| Pull request delivery | Git provider permissions, branch rules |

## Best practices

- Keep requests small enough for a human to review.
- Include acceptance criteria before generation starts.
- Treat validation failures as useful feedback, not only errors.
- Use logs and pull request checks to understand failed builds.
- Avoid asking for unrelated refactors in the same request as a feature.
